reference.method: Static inspection of the matched executable, public symbols, field layouts and virtual slots. No executable was run. This file contains metadata and bounded conclusions, not code bytes or disassembly.

facts.topic: ClickAir held-item descriptor is captured before local use
facts.contract: The baseUseItem population callback sets the transaction selected-item descriptor from the original stack before copying the stack and invoking local GameMode::useItem. If local use succeeds, it writes the modified copy to the selected hand. It does not refresh the transaction selected-item descriptor afterward. Therefore the recovered ordinary ClickAir selected-item field is a pre-use snapshot; the inventory action carries the old-to-new change.

facts.topic: Inventory change capture and unconditional client forwarding
facts.contract: baseUseItem wraps local use in a container transaction context. Its change callback constructs InventoryAction from old and new stacks, appends the pending player action and adds it to the complex transaction. The main-hand source is ordinary container0 with the reported slot; offhand is container119/slot0. The client forwards the complex transaction before consulting the callback success byte, so local failure does not itself suppress this sender.

facts.topic: Legacy request scope uses a current client screen
facts.contract: The client legacy-scope helper first obtains a current ClientScreenData. If no screen exists it returns a no-op scope. With a screen, it advances the legacy counter as min(counter,-2)-2, stores the resulting negative-even request ID and clears that screen changed-slot map. The scope cleanup resets the active request ID to0 and clears the map. The exact first observed ID depends on earlier counter use.

facts.topic: Ordinary selected inventory reaches the manager-aware setter
facts.contract: For selected container Inventory=0, Player::setCarriedItem forwards to PlayerInventory.mInventory at the selected slot. The concrete Inventory setter forwards to setItemWithForceBalance, which calls the manager-aware setPlayerContainer helper before falling back to FillingContainer. The helper callback also ends in FillingContainer. This closes the ordinary main-hand count-change call chain; it does not close every event listener or offhand path.

facts.topic: Nonempty changed stacks receive the active legacy ID in this client branch
facts.contract: setPlayerContainer rejects an invalid, null or zero-count proposed new stack before its client legacy branch. For a local player with an active negative-even legacy ID, a nonempty changed stack is copied, its ItemStackNetIdVariant is set to the legacy-request alternative carrying the active ID, the changed slot is registered, and the callback receives the tagged copy. An unchanged item/count returns without this mutation. Consequently retaining an old positive server stack ID while predicting a decrement is not equivalent to this recovered branch.

facts.topic: Changed-slot enum translation and empty-slot distinction
facts.contract: The client changed-slot callback translates legacy Inventory=-1 to InventoryContainer=29, Armor=18 to ArmorContainer=6, and Hand=19 to OffhandContainer=34; it records the slot as an unsigned byte. Unsupported legacy container kinds return. Empty proposed stacks take the caller fallback instead of this particular nonempty legacy-tagging path. This distinction matters for a last-item consumption and does not by itself prove all other listeners leave the changed-slot map empty.

facts.contract: LocalPlayer copies the active legacy request ID to the outgoing payload. Only negative-even IDs below-1 enter changed-slot collection. It copies per-screen container/slot sets into LegacySetSlot records. If that collected vector is empty, it resets the outgoing legacy request ID to0. Unordered containers do not establish a stable multi-slot ordering.

limits: These are matched protocol2193 control/data-flow facts. The protocol2225 executable was not assumed identical.

The native current HUD/request-screen creation and lifetime, all packet authority-mode gates, request acknowledgement/reconciliation and rollback were not reconstructed. The captured scope conditions must not be replaced with an unconditional locally invented request ID.
The complete wire-level net-ID/include-ID encoding and byte-for-byte inventory transaction serialization were not re-derived here. C++ layout is not a wire format.

Player::setCarriedItem also publishes an event before the selected-container mutation (call RVA0x2034CF -> RVA0x2FEA260); its full dynamic listener set was not traced. Offhand and custom container variants are outside this follow-up.

This artifact closes the prior held-item pre/post snapshot uncertainty and ordinary nonempty selected-slot call chain. It does not authorize claiming a complete pearl prediction implementation from a count decrement plus an empty action vector.

The empty-new-stack helper branch and outgoing empty-set reset are established individually; a global claim that every last-item use always emits legacyRequestId0 would require closing all contributing callbacks.
